bullets.title: NVDA: $105B Ohio Data Center Deal with OpenAI; Invests $1.5B in SB Energy
bullets.body: NVDA secured 4.25 IT-GW capacity at PORTS-Pike Technology Campus in Pike County, Ohio via SB Energy partnership, with OpenAI as 20-year lessee; deal could generate $150-200B in revenue over 20 years per midday summary. NVDA reduced its credit backstop from $250B to ~$120B to address balance sheet concerns while investing $1.5B directly into SB Energy. Operations begin 2028; SoftBank/SB Energy committed to building 10+ GW of new energy generation supporting 8 IT-GW of AI factory capacity.

bullets.title: NVDA Spectrum-X CPO in Mass Production; HBM4e Up 70-100%; Rubin De-Spec Could Sustain HBM Volume
bullets.body: NVIDIA's Spectrum-X CPO switches entered mass production targeting 15k units in 2026 and 100k in 2027, with TSMC expanding inspection capacity to support the ramp. HBM4e pricing is up 70-100%, and Rubin Ultra de-spec could expand total HBM chip circulation, sustaining demand for MU, Samsung, and SK Hynix. VR rack production on track for Sep-Dec 2026 with 2,500-3,000 NVL72 racks expected and >50k in 2027E.

bullets.title: MU/SNDK/Memory: AI-Driven HBM & NAND Demand Surges; SNDK +35% Post Investor Day
bullets.body: SNDK rallied 35%+ last week following an upbeat investor day showcasing BiCS10 QLC with ~60% higher bit density vs BiCS8, and JPMorgan upgraded to OW on AI-driven NAND demand and structural pricing inflection. DRAM spot prices rose W/W (DDR4 16Gb +1.4%), and NAND flash prices surged (256Gb TLC +17.5%). HBM and server memory remain supply-constrained under long-term contracts; SK Hynix's AI-HBM focus supports premium valuations vs Samsung's larger commodity DRAM exposure to Chinese competition.

bullets.title: CRWV: $104B Revenue Backlog, Nearly 2x Market Cap; GPU-Cloud Demand Durable
bullets.body: CoreWeave's revenue backlog stands at $104B, nearly 2x its current market cap, signaling exceptional demand visibility. Neo-cloud providers including CRWV are pushing short-term GPU contracts at premium pricing vs AWS long-term deals; 2020-era Ampere GPUs contracted through 2029 with useful life extended to 6-9 years per 22V Research.

bullets.title: SNAP: Down 15% on French Court Ruling Blocking Teen Social Media Ban
bullets.body: SNAP extended session losses to a low of -15% intraday after a French court blocked a ban on social media for children under 15, with Macron pushing reform until spring. StreetAccount also flagged SNAP trading on 109% unusual volume with no other company-specific news disclosed.

bullets.title: ALAB: Upgraded to Outperform; PT Raised to $350 from $225
bullets.body: Astralux Lab (ALAB) was upgraded to Outperform from Market Perform with a price target raised sharply to $350 from $225 by Northland Capital. The stock was among the biggest pre-market gainers at +6.1%.

bullets.title: AAPL: Upgraded to Buy; PT to $400 from $260 at Rothschild Redburn
bullets.body: Rothschild Redburn upgraded Apple from Neutral to Buy and raised its price target to $400 from $260, citing the 2.55B-device installed base, strong customer retention, and high-margin Services growth. Separately, the Trump Administration opposes Apple sourcing memory chips from China, a potential supply-chain headwind.

bullets.title: INTU: Mizuho Constructive Ahead of FQ4 Reset; PT Cut to $430 by Klein
bullets.body: Mizuho sees INTU trading at trough 13x FY27E non-GAAP P/E and expects management to reset FY27 expectations with incremental conservatism on the FQ4 call — a credibility-rebuilding clearing event. Klein also lowered PT to $430 (from higher) but reiterated Outperform, noting a September Investor Day follows earnings.

bullets.title: SNOW: Jefferies Raises PT to $385 from $310
bullets.body: Jefferies raised its Snowflake price target to $385 from $310, the largest of the PT moves flagged this morning. SNOW was noted as down modestly in pre-market alongside broader software weakness.

bullets.title: APP: Benchmark Cuts PT to $440 from $500; Jefferies Hosts Advertiser Expert Call
bullets.body: Benchmark cut AppLovin's price target to $440 from $500. Separately, Jefferies hosted an expert call with a DIFF Eyewear digital marketing VP discussing AppLovin's e-commerce ad ROAS vs. Meta/Google, with the advertiser ramping AppLovin spend and reviewing new generative AI campaign types.

bullets.title: GEV: 2.5 GW Gas+SMR Plant in Texas; Record 2Q Turbine Orders Up 71% Y/Y
bullets.body: GE Vernova signed agreement with Blue Energy for a 2.5 GW combined gas and SMR plant in Victoria, TX targeting 2030 data center capacity delivery, with five BWRX-300 SMRs adding ~1.5 GW from 2032. Q2 global turbine orders rose 71% Y/Y to a record; JPM estimates ~85 GW global OEM capacity by 2028 and sets a YE27 PT of $1,330.

bullets.title: EQIX/DLR: Relatively Protected from Data Center Community Pushback Per MS; 13F Bullish
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley sees EQIX and DLR as relatively protected from data center political headwinds given scale, critical-infrastructure status, and community engagement track records — both have accelerated development and raised capex guidance. 13F filings show Duquesne and Coatue buying EQIX, while Elliott liquidated its CCI short and covered DLR puts.

bullets.title: VST: Most Advantaged IPP on Data Center Demand Per MS Byrd; Softer ERCOT Forwards Modest Negative
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Stephen Byrd views VST as the most advantaged independent power producer given ERCOT interconnection process confirmation of demand. However, softer 2027-28 ERCOT forward prices are a marginal negative for VST and CEG, while prolonged grid uncertainty is bullish for onsite power plays (SEI, BE).

bullets.title: NFLX: MS AlphaWise Flags Accelerating Post-Price-Hike Churn; PT $90 (~22% Upside)
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's AlphaWise survey found Netflix's March 2026 price increase triggered meaningfully higher churn versus prior cycles, suggesting increased subscriber price sensitivity. MS lowered its NFLX PT to $90 (~22% upside at ~22x NTM EPS) with a bear case of $60 (~20% downside, 15x).

bullets.title: MSFT: Stands Out as Clearest Publicly Traded GenAI Beneficiary Per MS CIO Survey
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's CIO survey identified Microsoft as the clearest publicly traded beneficiary of GenAI spending, agentic automation, and custom AI applications. CIO budgets improving with +3.8% growth expected in 2026, the first up-to-down ratio above 1.0x since 1Q24.

bullets.title: ADI: Q3 Earnings Preview — Consensus $3.92B Rev, $3.34 EPS; Wolfe Bullish on Price Hikes
bullets.body: ADI reports Q3 earnings 8/19 before open; consensus expects $3.92B revenue and $3.34 EPS (72.5% gross margin), with options implying ~6.3% post-earnings move. Wolfe Research sees ADI implementing aggressive HSD% price increases next year, targeting potential $17 EPS in CY27, with Street likely underestimating upside.

bullets.title: AMZN: MS Sees AWS Hitting $1T Revenue in 8-10 Years; Trainium 4 at 5M Units by H2 2027
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley reiterates Overweight on AMZN ($335 PT) with analyst Brian Nowak projecting AWS could reach $1T in revenue within 8-10 years from current price of $262.65. AWS Trainium 4 chip adoption is forecast at 5M units in H2 2027 and 12M units in 2028, with three configurations expected.

bullets.title: RBLX: Citi Buy; Week 33 CCUs Up 6% Sequentially, 3Q26 Bookings Tracking Above Guidance
bullets.body: Citi maintains Buy on Roblox; Week 33 average peak CCUs were 17.1M (down 17% Y/Y but up 6% sequentially). Projected 3Q26 bookings of $1.68B track just above the company's $1.65B guidance high-end, though bookings per payer are modeled lower at $51 vs $58 in 2Q26.

bullets.title: SHOP: Downgraded at Phillips Securities; Down 2.7% in Canada Trading
bullets.body: Shopify was downgraded at Phillips Securities and fell 2.7% (C$208.50, -C$5.85) in Canada mid-morning trading, adding to its pre-market weakness noted in the US session.

bullets.title: OKLO: Upgraded to Overweight; LYV Featured as MS Non-AI Best Idea
bullets.body: OKLO was upgraded from Equal Weight to Overweight this morning. Separately, Morgan Stanley highlighted Live Nation (LYV) as an Overweight non-AI best idea with idiosyncratic earnings catalysts, in a webcast alongside FWONK, TKO, DIS, and SPHR in its 'Live 5' media framework.
